rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Judgment, full sequential read of chunks 0-9. Nearest candidate: chunk 5 "Feedback-loopable methodology..." line 62 "Amp changed its mind about the whole mechanism" — "the whole mechanism" resolves to the Handoff feature named two sentences earlier in the same chunk (line 60). Chunk 9's practitioner references (Klaassen, Pocock, Yan/Cognition, Metcalf/Amp, Cherny, Cognition) at lines 139-143 all reuse names introduced in their own earlier chunks of this same file — protected by the rule's own carve-out ("a term introduced on an earlier slide of the same file and reused"). No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found anywhere in the body.

grep -niE for body-scoped file-position phrasing ("opening lecture", "the top of this page") returns 0 body hits (the only "Pairs with lectures/composing-the-workflow.md" cross-file line lives in the maintainer meta note, line 162, outside the body region). Every in-body link names its target by title (line 24 '[Compound Engineering plugin...]', line 133 '[Dino's skill stacking system]'), never by position.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Every chunk (0-9) carries a substantial, standalone claim or catalogue entry; none is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet. Chunk 0 (lines 1-4, title+lede) is the exempt title slide.

Checked every chunk header against its own content under the cover-then-uncover test: each practitioner-named header (e.g. line 54 'Feedback-loopable methodology and shipped primitives, Sourcegraph Amp') is a true, literal summary of what follows in that chunk. No header is contradicted by its own body.

grep -niE for the 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction → 0 matches. Nearest anaphora candidate: chunk 9 lines 139 and 141 ('If you're shipping...', 'If you're already shipping...', 'If your team is wrestling...', 'If your team has standardised...' / 'Klaassen is heavy...Pocock is light...Cognition is somewhere in between') — each leg names a distinct practitioner plus distinct concrete criteria (new content per leg), which is exactly the carve-out the rule states ('third leg carries NEW concrete content') rather than the banned vacuous-repetition shape. No self-grading superlatives (grep for 'one of the (most|best)' → 0 hits), no abstraction-noun stacks, no empty-leg verb triplets found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -niE '\b(surface|firing|compendium|forcing function|beat|mood|Connections)\b' on the body → 1 hit, line 79 'agent picks up the human's existing tool surface.' Judgment: 'tool surface' here parallels ordinary SWE vocabulary ('API surface', 'attack surface'), not the repo's internal 'writing surface'/curriculum-authoring sense the rule's lead example names. AE101's audience is engineer ICs, for whom this reads as shop vocabulary, per the rule's own audience-register weighing clause.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 8 "Skill stacking system, Dino: the worked example": lines 117-119 ("**A single orchestrator** by deliberate design.", "**Phase-organised skill catalogue.**", "**Design principles** the system enforces.") and lines 123-126 ("**Front-loaded read-only analysis.**", "**Mandatory gates fire positionally**", "**Re-invocation as control flow.**", "**CLAUDE.md as half the system.**") — two separate bulleted lists on one slide where every bullet opens with a bolded lead, plus a standalone bold at line 128 ("**scales cross-repo**"). 8 non-navigational bold spans on a single chunk against the ≤1-per-slide budget (chunk 9's 'filter questions' at lines 139/141/143 are explicitly exempted by this same rule's own text as this file's named calibration example, so they are excluded from this finding). This is the rule's own named violation shape ('every bullet on a slide opens with a bolded sentence... flatten to handles or prose'), not covered by the lookup-surface carve-out, which applies to prose-paragraph entries, not bulleted label+prose rows like these.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Flatten the two Dino bullet lists (lines 117-119, 123-126) to plain prose leads or unbolded bullets, keeping at most one bolded handle per list (or per slide) rather than bolding every item.
